cands.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 28th District since 2009. Psychologist who taught psychology in the Los Angeles Community College District for 20 years. Previously served on the Garvey school board, Monterey Park City Council (three-time mayor), State Assembly (2001-2006) and State Board of Equalization.

controversies.text: In December 2014 the House Ethics Committee issued Chu a public letter of reproval for interfering with its investigation of campaign work by her staff. It found her two top aides had directed staff to do campaign work on official time, but found no evidence Chu knew. Chu said she regretted contacting her staff.
Missed 2 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (0.3%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 1, 2025-01-09 to 2025-01-09.

endorsements.text: 2026: Democratic Party of California; California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO; California Teachers Association; California Environmental Voters; Equality California; Sierra Club Angeles Chapter.

cands.gaps: We found no stated positions or actions from Chu on development and growth limits, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, gun laws, school choice or teacher pay, police pay, or H-1B visas. Her own words on the Monterey Park data-center measure were not available, only a listing that she supports it. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. Where her pages describe her time on the Monterey Park council and as mayor, the exact years differ slightly between sources. The Wikipedia page we read did not cover her recent elections or recent terms.

cands.name: April A. Verlato

money.note: Individuals gave $700; PAC money $0; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Arcadia, California attorney and businesswoman. Elected to the Arcadia City Council in 2016 and served as mayor beginning in 2020. Republican candidate for California's 28th Congressional District in 2024 and 2026, losing to incumbent Judy Chu both times.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California (listed for her 2024 race)

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements from Verlato on data centers, development or growth limits, foreign or institutional buying of homes and land, gun policy, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no council vote records, so her claims about her council votes on policing could not be checked. Her campaign website's issue pages and endorsements page were not available in full; the home page only gave headline themes. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026. Her policy statements come from a 2024 campaign website text quoted by Ballotpedia, and we found nothing newer. We found no news coverage, controversies or foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia says she was born and raised in Arcadia, California, and she has served on its city council and as mayor.

score.why: Raised $700, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Attorney (UCLA political science degree, Southwestern School of Law) and businesswoman. Arcadia city councilmember elected in 2016, then mayor beginning in 2020.
qual.why: Local elected office (council and mayor) plus a legal career fits the middle band for lawmaking, oversight and budgeting. She has no experience at the state or federal level.
qual.label: Local elected office (council and mayor) plus a legal career fits the middle band for lawmaking, oversight and budgeting. She has no experience at the state or federal level.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign website says she voted every year of her council service to support the police chief's plans, ordinances and budget requests, and voted to add 4 sworn officers in Arcadia. This is her own claim, and no council records were available to confirm it.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Her campaign website says she supports full reinstatement of Prop 13's provisions and signed the Taxpayer Protection Pledge.

workers-first.evidence: Her campaign website says the federal government has a duty to enforce laws at the border, and she lists securing the border as a priority. It does not address H-1B visas.
